newsitem.title: USA: USDA readying new export loan regulations-official.
newsitem.headline: USDA readying new export loan regulations-official.

text.p: Agriculture Department staffers are working to develop rules on new so-called facility loans to help countries import more agricultural commodities, and the department proposal will hopefully be published the first of next year, said a USDA official.

Mary Chambliss, deputy administrator for export credits with USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service, said the new facility loans will aid in developing import facilities, infrastructure, refrigeration, and other services.
The longterm loans will go to the private sector, and were authorized under the farm bill as part of USDA's GSM loan program.

Chambliss, speaking at a conference on EU enlargement with Eastern European nations, said the department hopes to have the proposed rules on the new loan program to the Office of Management and Budget within the next 4-6 weeks, and to have the rules published in January.

Chambliss told reporters that the department is also discussing a new program under PL-480 to enter into longterm loans with a private entity, instead of the traditional government-to-government approach.

Chambliss said it will probably be several months before USDA has a proposal prepared, but that the new authority would be a way to work with "scarce" government resources to promote private development.
